title: Interview with Sergey Vasylchuk from Everstake at Consensus 2024
text:
[0:14] Dylan, Podcast Host: Hey guys, Dylan from the Smart Economy podcast. We're at day 2 at Consensus 2024 here in Austin, Texas, and I'm chatting with Sergey Vasilchuk, the CEO, co-founder, you name it, at EverStake. How's it going, Sergey?
[0:27] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Yeah, nice to meet you guys. I'm fine. Good time, good market. Happy to see you.
[0:32] Dylan, Podcast Host: So yesterday we got to catch up a little bit, and it was awesome. You recognized my name tag because of the Neo News Today stuff, but basically EverStake secures a ton of different blockchain networks. So for anyone who's never heard of what you guys do and who you are, what's like your elevator pitch? What do you do, and what networks do you secure?
[0:52] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: So, like, we secure basically all the proof-of-stake blockchains. And, like, our goal is to make it sustainable, fast, and we just sign your transactions. Whatever transaction you sign, we're like most of the blockchains. There is a very high probability that we're the guy who signed your transaction. So we're technically your gateway to the blockchain.
[1:14] Dylan, Podcast Host: And does it need to be proof-of-stake? Because we're starting to enter a world where there's, like, various different types of validator models, and maybe that is within or outside of your purview.
[1:25] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Like, it depends. Like, if you see, like, we support like 100 of the blockchains. I suppose, like, I hope that we'll be like another 200, and each of them will find a specific niche. So the way how and the reason why we started the EverStake, because I was thinking and assuming that in order to be fast, fast enough, we need to have the professional validators, professional parties, like, to make a great job.
[1:51] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah.
[1:51] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: And, like, my bet wasright. And for the most of the, like, DeFi or fast-performing blockchains, like, we really need the validators.
[2:01] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yes. So I think what's super cool about EverStake is whenever I'm trying out a new blockchain ecosystem, I have a name that I can trust when I want to stake and validate. So what are your kind of criteria for which blockchains? Because you guys support 100 blockchains, but there are thousands of them. So what do you look for in a new blockchain ecosystem when you want to provide validation services?
[2:26] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Well, like, our credo, like, is to be useful. So, like, we have some expertise, like, in many of the fields. Unfortunately, another, like, 200 of the blockchains were already dead. But they went from our hands, and, like, at least we know what not to do.
[2:40] Dylan, Podcast Host: Right.
[2:41] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: And, like, we have this, like, gut feeling already. And, like, of course we have some, like, research and scientific, like, approach. But, like, gut feelings, like, also tell us, like, what, like, chains we need to select, what not, what to skip. And, like, it's simple, less like ABC. Like, if we find the way to be useful there, like, we join. If not, like, we cannot, like, be everywhere.
[3:03] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah. And, like, so you guys are more than just being useful for, like, providing technical solutions. You guys also educate communities. So, like, what are ways in which EverStake thinks that as a company you can be useful to token holders and to blockchain ecosystems in general? What are the sort of resources you guys provide beyond just staking?
[3:24] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Yeah, like, it's, again, like, be useful. But you can be useful for the partners, like, for other blockchain partners. You can be useful for the investors. You can be useful for the customers. And, like, I never forget, like, my institute and, like, my math teacher said to me, like, hey guys, you're not stupid. You're just, like, uneducated. But my job is to fix it.
[3:42] Dylan, Podcast Host: Right.
[3:43] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: So sometimes when I, like, see, like, come to the new, like, community and blockchain and see, like, the people, like, are a bit, like, uneducated, I say, okay, we can fix it. So this is, like, the way how we try to be useful, like, for the, like, wider audience. So the more education we're doing, like, the better, like, for us, for our customers, and for the global community. So it's tough. It's a long way. But, like, it's payoff.
[4:05] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah. So, like, what's on the roadmap? What is EverStake going to be looking at next? Do you guys already have, like, some blockchain networks you're looking to support? Are there new services you guys are going to start integrating? What's, like, something to look forward to?
[4:19] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Well, the good news for us and, like, the community in total, that, like, we have the rise of the, like, up chain. This means, like, the project would try, like, to find its market fit on the public chain, but then, like, it's become expensive or it's become, like, very, like, narrowed down with the performance. Like, on this, they start, like, to deploy in its own chain. Cosmos-based, Solana-based, Forke whatever. So we'll see, like, just a ton of them. And, like, we try to be in those blockchains which require, like, the high performance.
[4:51] Dylan, Podcast Host: Right.
[4:52] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: So, like, we really have the, like, a backlog of the hundreds of the hundreds projects. And we try to scale, like, with the human resources as well, but it's not easy.
[5:01] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah.
[5:02] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: But so when we acquire, like, new talents, when we acquire, like, new engineers, like, we train them because we try to be useful for our employees as well. So, like, it's a long process. So, like, scaling, like, is good problems to solve, but, like, it's a challenging problem.
[5:18] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah. So is this your first Consensus?
[5:21] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: No, like, it's not our first Consensus. Like, we're mostly, like, visiting, like, Consensus, like, time to time. But this is the first time, like, we put the booth and we just try to attract, like, the people, real people to touch the grass.
[5:36] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yes.
[5:37] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Yeah, like, to listen, like, their voice, to, like, answer the question, like, and to send, like, the feeling, the problems. So we just, like, like, got him, like, down to the ground and, like, and talk to the people.
[5:49] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah, it was awesome running into your booth. So what have the conversations been like? Are you meeting, like, long-term users of your network?
[5:55] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: You cannot even imagine, like, what the diversity of the question they are. So, like, hey, like, what are you doing, like, stake? What is stake? Okay, like, we need to educate ourselves. Another, like, partners came, like, for other blockchains, and, like, we have some, like, very, like, technical, like, detailed, like, conversation. Another guy's, like, coming, like, technical better, say, like, hey, how do you attract, like, 800,000 customers? Can you help me? Like, I want to be, like, with it as well. So, like, just, like, random question.
[6:25] Dylan, Podcast Host: So this isn't your first Consensus. So what's, like, the vibe like? How have the conversations and the energy at previous different Consensuses, what have they been like compared to where we're at at Consensus 2024 today?
[6:41] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Well, like, maybe this answer will be disappointed, but nothing significantly will change.
[6:48] Dylan, Podcast Host: That's not disappointing.
[6:49] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Yeah, so people, like, still, like, asking, like, dumb questions. People still, like, are lazy, like, to educate themselves. And, but, like, it's less about the crypto in general, like, human behavior. Yeah.
[7:02] Dylan, Podcast Host: Right.
[7:03] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: We use, like, to consume, like, information from the TV or YouTube, whatever, and still, like, people want to become the rich tomorrow.
[7:11] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yes.
[7:12] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: But, like, don't want, like, to spend the time to see, like, what is going on. And they become the victim, like, of the scammers. So unfortunately, I don't see, like, the, like, elevation of the, like, knowledge. We're still, like, on the same, like, uneducated level.
[7:27] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah, yeah. But, like, globally, do you feel like there's a positive for where we're going as an industry? Do you see a potential change for educating the average user?
[7:38] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Like, I, like, the most exciting thing that, like, happened, I believe, like, at least, like, in my perception, that we see that even the American government, like, lists for the voice. And the reason why they put, like, it's, like, political, like, ETF and all this, like, deal decision, because they see the mass, like, of the crypto people, which they, like, take into account. Yeah?
[8:01] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah.
[8:02] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: So congrats, guys. Like, our, like, our numbers is already, like, significant to make, like, US even policy, like, take into account. I believe, and I hope, and, like, we contribute to make us not just the quantity, but the quality. And then, like, we will be like quantity and the quality, quality and the education. We can, we can win.
[8:23] Dylan, Podcast Host: Awesome.
[8:23] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: So let's work on this.
[8:24] Dylan, Podcast Host: Yeah. Well, let's do it. Sergey, your booth has been busy every time I've walked around. So congratulations on always having people here. And you're super busy on your computer, so I want to thank you for taking some time to talk with us, to share some insights into what you're working on.
[8:38] Sergey Vasylchuk, CEO and Co-founder of Everstake: Thank you. Thank you.
[8:40] Dylan, Podcast Host: Cheers. And of course, if you want to see any of the other interviews that we've done here at Consensus 2024, head over to Neo News Today's YouTube page to see more of the live interviews. And if you want to hear any of the full-length podcast episodes we've done, head over to SmartEconomyPodcast.com.

title: How Everstake Became the Biggest Staking Provider | Anna Petrenko -  Everstake | GM Podcast
text:
[0:03] Zach, Podcast Host: Hey, what's up—this is Zach here at the Gen Z on Media House, the GN Podcast in Bangkok, Thailand. Super excited to be talking about staking. I'll let our next guest introduce herself. If you want to say your name, the company you're with, and your position at the company.
[0:20] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Uh, yeah, for sure. Nice to meet you. My name is Anna, I'm head of R&D at EverStake, and we are the biggest one staking provider.
[0:28] Zach, Podcast Host: Wow, okay, that's amazing. You say "the biggest" staking provider?
[0:32] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Uh, yeah, the biggest one staking provider for the number of our users. So we have 735,000 unique users, I mean stakers, so yeah, and it feels pretty, pretty good to deliver our service to the community.
[0:47] Zach, Podcast Host: Very cool. So I think R&D is very interesting, and I find it fascinating that you are on the podcast, because we usually don't get to speak to people who are interested in R&D on camera. So kind of, what is that like, being in, you know, R&D in the staking?
[1:04] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: So it's pretty interesting, because we are in R&D, taking care of all the new projects that appear on the market. So we conduct an R&D research, doing our modeling—project lifecycle modeling, economic modeling—and talk to the project team and decide if this project is promising enough. So EverStake can join on an operational level as a validator, I mean, and support the project and deliver the service for staking to the community. So it's like deep research work, and we are feel excited on this part because it's allowed to get some insight, to get some, like, correlations, and still have a deep dive in project economics and model it. So pretty cool.
[1:52] Zach, Podcast Host: No, I completely agree. And I think we were chatting before, can you talk about maybe some of the ecosystems that you guys support? Because I know there's a lot of different projects.
[2:04] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah, definitely. So the biggest one, I believe, is Cicero, for sure.
[2:08] Zach, Podcast Host: I think people have probably heard of that, yeah.
[2:10] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah, yeah, yeah. So it's pretty good as it appears on different levelsright now. So it's Cicero, native staking, liquid staking, re-staking. Actually, we're operating on all of these three levels at EverStake, and it's quite different target audience on each of them. So some levels are mostly institutional, some levels are mostly for retail, and some, like, newly appearance level, like re-staking, is pretty excited also for both parts. So we are deep inside on a, like, database scientific level of researching and modeling that's the most, like, hot topics here. So what will be the APR for re-staking, how the session will works there, so how the service will works there for, like, end users, and what you can expect and what you can achieve. So this is a case, for sure, like bull shark-based projects feel pretty excited. So I mean, it's like captives, it's UE projects, newly appeared Aleo, very nice L1 project as well. So yeah, we're also expecting a few more strong L1 projects this year, so it will be the first quarter they should launch their main net.
[3:34] Zach, Podcast Host: Any you want to shout out that you're excited for?
[3:38] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Um, yeah, why not. So we're expecting the particle network.
[3:42] Zach, Podcast Host: Oh yeah, particle, that's a big one.
[3:45] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah, this is for the main net launch, Wallet Connect network. Actually, yesterday they announced the official date of staking launch, I believe it's end of November. What else? It's a few test nets, like Walrus test nets, just launched, Space and Time test net will be launched very soon, I believe this quarter as well. So yeah, and a few more, like Story Protocol, Beaver Chain, expected next phases of Babylon as well. So pretty wide range and different types of projects in the top rate.
[4:25] Zach, Podcast Host: What do you think that people don't understand about staking? Like, what's a common misconception that you think you hear that people should know?
[4:35] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Um, the most common? So it depends on the type of user we talk about. So for institutional, it's different types of concerns and miscommunications and misunderstandings. For the retail, the most part, I believe it's the difference between staking and DeFi projects and products that appear on the market. So where end users should understand that if he stakes, he helps to secure the ecosystem, and he helps to secure the blockchain itself with his funds. So he stakes to validator on a proof of stake concept and helps to secure the blockchain. And on a DeFi project, it's a different type of activity and, like, earning specific income. So it's like very, very different structure here. So it's like the most, the most common, I guess.
[5:33] Zach, Podcast Host: Which one would you say, I mean, I—this is probably odd—what is the one you say is safer? Like, why do you think? Because I think staking is much, much safer. I mean, and sort of securing the blockchain. Can you kind of explain that to people who maybe don't understand?
[5:47] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Uh, yeah, for sure. It's linked to the concept how proof of stake networks work itself. So it's a set of validators, each validator running their nodes, yeah, on the technical level of operations. And so users can stake their money to the validator. So it's like non-custodial, fully non-custodial way. And with the stake, validator produce the blocks on the network, so on the blockchain itself, and confirm the transactions. And the blockchain exists according to this part. And actually, it's allowed to get it move with the blocks forward, and it's allowed to prevent any malicious actions in the blockchain for, like, any validators or other malicious players.
[6:42] Zach, Podcast Host: No, I think that's really important. I think—thank you for breaking that down, because a lot of people talk about it, and you actually broke it down, like, very eloquently. So I really appreciate that. Can you maybe talk about, like, what the advantage is for staking with you guys versus maybe another platform? Like, you know, say I have, like, a million dollars to stake, why would I stake with you guys?
[7:06] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Um, I believe it depends mostly on the technical level of operations. So it should be, it should be a trusted party. So it not depends you will choose EverStake or any other. It should be a trusted party. And it's important to hold all the operations in-house. So for example, in EverStake, we have around 60 people in the develop staff. So we hold all our operations in-house, and our uptime is 99.9%. So it's—
[7:34] Zach, Podcast Host: Happens the other 0.1. No, just kidding, just kidding.
[7:37] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: It depends on the consensus mechanism.
[7:39] Zach, Podcast Host: Just kidding, yeah. That's very good.
[7:41] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: It's actually, it's important because, you know, some consensus mechanism allowed to keep, like, 100% uptime, and some consensus mechanism, it's very good. If it's, like, 99 there, it's like top achievement.
[7:56] Zach, Podcast Host: Got you.
[7:56] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah. So yeah, technical level of operations is very important. And the quality of nodes, backup servers, strict security policy, strict technical policy of operations. So it should be like a trusted provider that could guarantee you as an end user that it will be top performed. And you should be interested in this part not only for, like, some slashes or some losing of your money, and also for, like, a top APR. Because as better the performance of staking providers, the better APR you will get as an end user.
[8:34] Zach, Podcast Host: And that's really, I mean, that's key,right? You always want to go where the APR is the highest and, of course, the most secure.
[8:41] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yes.
[8:42] Zach, Podcast Host: That's super interesting. What, I guess, for you with the market kind of like pumpingright now, there's obviously a lot of new capital coming into crypto, what do you see the future of staking? Like, where do you see this market going in the next 5, even 10 years?
[8:59] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Oh, I believe it's hard to say for, like, 10 years.
[9:03] Zach, Podcast Host: Even years, let's say 6 months.
[9:05] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah, yeah. Yeah, so we actually predicting and conducting our market research in depth for, like, one year ahead. And yeah, we expecting some interesting trends coming on the market. So for sure, for sure, re-staking will developed, and we'll expect the expand to other ecosystem. It will be not only Ceroom. We expect Solana ecosystem re-staking quite some high level. Also, it's like BTC, BTC re-staking and walled projects. So we expect on Symbiotic, Babylon, DLC BTC, and some other projects will be strong on this part.
[9:48] Zach, Podcast Host: Why do you think BTC staking is so low as a percentage of market cap compared to, like, Ethereum?
[9:54] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Uh, because it's only, only emerging trend. So it's just started, let's say, a year or a year and a half ago. And the projects on BTC staking, re-staking is pretty youngright now. And it also depends on the project quality, you know, because it's when it's a load of, like, smart contracts inside, when it's very long road inside there, it couldn't be, like, trusted or secure enough to participate in, I mean, for big players. So we should wait to it to stabilize a bit. And we should wait for some, like, big projects, stable projects. So we'll launch their main nets with BTC staking, and we expect that this direction should grow enough on the market.
[10:48] Zach, Podcast Host: Do you see particular companies moving in that direction?
[10:53] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: For BTC staking? Uh, yeah, sure. We expect in Babylon, it's already launched on main net, it should be, like, another cap opening soon. We're looking closely for Symbiotic and also operate on Symbiotic, and it should be BTC vaults inside there with the different options with, like, good trusted market players. I mean, LRTs and all the related stuff should run in this part. Also, some, like, XR, DLC BTC, core projects. So pretty strong, and I think they will get quite huge market share.
[11:33] Zach, Podcast Host: I completely agree. I think XR, the one that you called out, is really cool. We work with them, and I think they're doing an excellent job.
[11:39] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Oh, yeah, we actually operate on an XR as well, so.
[11:42] Zach, Podcast Host: Oh, very cool. So mutual, mutual connections there. Yeah, those guys are great. Kind of bringing it back to where we are here, which is in Thailand. How has the event been for you so far? What's kind of the goal for the team here, if there is one? Or if not, just having fun, because it is very fun.
[12:01] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah.
[12:02] Zach, Podcast Host: I know there's a lot of work to be done, so.
[12:04] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah, yeah, it's a lot of work, actually. It's a lot of stuff to do. It's a lot of our partners here. So it's like 900 side events during this week.
[12:15] Zach, Podcast Host: Yeah, I read something that said if the average side event is like 10 grand, that's $9 million spent on side events this week. Isn't that crazy?
[12:26] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah, it's amazing.
[12:27] Zach, Podcast Host: Yeah, $9 million spent in Thailand. So they obviously love having the event here. If you think about all the money that's coming in, but sorry to interrupt, but yeah, it is crazy.
[12:35] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah, yeah, definitely. Definitely. And, you know, it's expected to be a lot of, a lot of people here and a lot of new projects here. So we have mostly our, like, partners meetings here from R&D side, I mean. And we are hosting, co-hosting two events. So please join us. It will be tomorrow, AVS Café with Sandeep. And it should be ASD, should be pretty huge with consensus. And it should be almost all AVS is on re-staking level and some debate. So should be very active. I feel pretty excited on this part. Yeah, so welcome, please join us.
[13:19] Zach, Podcast Host: What's the debate on?
[13:22] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Debates, it will be like four different tracks for the debate. First, the debates for ours one, it will be the most hottest topic, I believe, in re-staking. It will be regarding slashing, regarding centralization on the re-staking part, and operation of on the market with, like, multiple AVSs for operators. So I believe it's the most discussable part of re-stakingright now, because everybody feel excited and guessing how the slashing conditions will look like and how users can manage the risk on this part and how to prevent some not desirable situation on this part and what to expect, etc., etc. So yeah, we will have pretty, pretty nice players here. It will be like consensus team, it will be out there team, EverStake team as well, and we will try to figure out the best, the best solutions and keys.
[14:28] Zach, Podcast Host: That's amazing. And kind of how big? You said there's 60 folks on the companyright now. How many of them are in Thailandright now from your team?
[14:37] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: So our team in total is 120 people.
[14:39] Zach, Podcast Host: Oh, 120. Okay, cool.
[14:41] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Yeah. And in Thailand, we have five people this year.
[14:45] Zach, Podcast Host: Okay, awesome. No, I think that's super cool. I know some teams have gotten together here and stuff, and it's really a fun place to kind of reconnect with your team, I found. Well, cool. Well, I just wanted to ask kind of as a closing, where can people find you on socials? Where's the best way to connect or to learn more?
[15:05] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Um, yeah, for sure. We covering almost all possible social media. So please, it's EverStake pool in Twitter, EverStake One websites, and all the LinkedTree, like LinkedIn, etc., etc., podcasts and all the other media. So we also have our own Discord for user support. So if you have any questions, EverStake website, Discord, please reach out to. We'll be happy to connect.
[15:30] Zach, Podcast Host: Thank you. Thank you so much for the amazing interview. Really appreciate the time and the information. Honestly, I really love that someone from also that you can research came on, because 99% of people cannot get into the level of detail that you did, and you explained it extremely well. So I really thank you for that, because for our audience, that is gold,right? Like, that is, that is literally why we do this, is to break down these concepts and to give people the understanding. So, you know, people really appreciate that. So thank you. And I hope you all enjoyed watching. So see you guys soon.
[16:04] Anna, Head of R&D at Everstake: Thank you so much.
[16:04] Zach, Podcast Host: Thank you.

[16:07] Speaker 4: But it's not something Gen Z is afraid of.
[16:09] Speaker 3: If you want to survive, you got to build a house.

[16:13] Speaker 3: Because we do not understand.

title: How to stake Ethereum starting from 0.1 ETH with Everstake Staking Dashboard
text: [0:01] Speaker 1: In this video, we'll show you how to stake Ethereum using the Everstake staking dashboard. To get started, click the "Connect Wallet" button. Next, choose the wallet you want to use. In this example, we'll connect the MetaMask wallet. Once your wallet is connected, the dashboard will display your available Ethereum balance. Now enter the amount of Ethereum you would like to stake. Please note that the minimum staking amount is 0.1 Ethereum. You can also click "Stake Max" to automatically select the maximum available amount. Before continuing, make sure to read and accept the terms and conditions by checking the box. When everything is ready, click "Stake Now." Then confirm the transaction in your wallet. After the transaction is confirmed, your tokens will be successfully staked, and you will start earning rewards based on the current reward rate. You can track it on the dashboard.
